Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Justin Kluivert scored Bournemouth’s second goal against Nottingham Forest three minutes into first-half added time. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images Premier League Bournemouth’s Evanilson and Kluivert sink Forest to make it nine wins in a row
 Press Association Sat 21 Nov 2026 12.10 EST Last modified on Sat 21 Nov 2026 14.20 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Marco Rose saluted the in-form Evanilson after the Brazilian scored for a sixth Premier League game in a row to lift Bournemouth up to fourth place with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest .
 Evanilson’s brilliantly taken 19th-minute opener set his side on course for a club-record ninth straight win in all competitions, while the defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win over Manchester City before the international break.
 Rose said: “We defend together as a team, and we attack together as a team, but the forward guys were excellent today. They did a great job scoring the goals and the other guys support them. Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a number nine, really beautiful goals so I am happy.”
 Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva.
 Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels.
 View image in fullscreen Nottingham Forest captain, Morgan Gibbs-White controls the ball under pressure from Bournemouth players. Photograph: Peter Nicholls/Getty Images Bournemouth took the lead through Evanilson in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-footed shot into the roof of the net.
 Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from the edge of the penalty area which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area.
 Quick Guide Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest: key facts
 Show • Bournemouth have won five successive games in the top-flight of English football for the first time. Only Arsenal (67, before Newcastle game) and Manchester City (60) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than the Cherries (52 – W13 D13 L4).
 • Bournemouth have won each of their last nine games in all competitions, their longest ever such run, overtaking two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.
 • Nottingham Forest failed to score in this game despite registering 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season. Opta 
 Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback. Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of team-mate Tyler Adams. But Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier.
 Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to forage a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for Morgan Gibbs-White but the captain could not properly connect with his header.
 James McAtee ballooned an effort over the crossbar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. The substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested the underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper, Dorde Petrovic.

Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.
 Glasner, whose side had 19 shots but only one on target, said: “Of course when you lose it’s always a tough 90 minutes, especially when you make too many mistakes like we did in the first half.
 “The second goal straight before half-time was a little bit of a killer but credit to the lads in the second half for finding a filter back into the game. We had some good situations, but we couldn’t convert them.
 “We are not able to score in this game, and this is what we have to look at and where we have to improve. We took too many touches, and were not so aggressive.”
